holes.hole: Battery attacks are open-loop edits of the reference's command list, and the lenient Runner tolerates refusals. An attack whose edited command is refused still 'fails', so it counts as met even though the cheat never happened. The reverse also happens: a refused undo leaves the reference's end state, so the run passes and the spec gets a false alarm. Nothing checks that the attack's intended effect took place. 9.1 says 'fails' needs a label 'acceptable for the policy', 9.4 says any label except budget, and neither defines the per-family labels. This repeats review class 10 (failing for incidental reasons) inside the battery itself.
holes.example_game: T-d389e2979f6aad-01, B3 `floor`: the trace has walked to {can} in the kitchen. The edited deposit targets the floor of the room 'adjacent by first connection id', which is not reachable from there, so it is refused. The robot ends holding the loaded dustpan and fails on house.held or the goal. B3 is recorded as met even if the conservation code were missing. T-f7f4105ce49060-01, B6 `undo_last`: the inverse pick_up / drop at the pre-deposit placement has no approach step, so it is refused. The screws stay sorted, the run passes, and the spec FAILS G3 for the battery's own bug. The author learns to file `event_goal` exemptions.
holes.fix: After every battery run, check that the attack happened: the mess parcel is at the swapped destination, the alternative member was acted on, the undone field is back at its baseline. Otherwise the run is `inconclusive`, and inconclusive counts as unmet. Generate attacks at skill level, inserting approach/goto before edited deposits and inverses. Define accepted labels per family: B3 must fail on house.mess_* / house.misplaced / the destination goal label, never only on house.held or budget. B6 must fail on the undone goal label.

holes.hole: Nothing checks false negatives. Every new rule only makes specs stricter, and the strength score rewards strictness. Several parts are fitted to the one reference: the envelope draft comes from its footprint, `to` scopes are its exact final placements, budgets come from its privileged routing, speech scoring is limited to the lexicon, and settle_s is fixed. So a HARDENED spec may be solvable only by the reference's way of doing the task, and no stage would notice.
holes.example_game: T-d389e2979f6aad-01: the draft envelope becomes `{earring}: {to: [{counter}]}` (the reference's pickup_to). An agent that hands the gold earring to its owner resident_1, or puts it on the dining table, fails house.misplaced:earring, although the instruction never says where it goes. Under realistic perception, an agent that uses a different broom or the second dustpan gets house.soiled / house.moved on an id the envelope did not list.
holes.fix: Add a must-pass battery that is the mirror of the cheat battery. Generate legitimate variants and require them to pass: another fungible instance or tool of the same type; a non-target item put at baseline, home or with its owner instead of the reference's spot; independent steps reordered; harmless extra look/inspect and detours inside the budget slack; speech paraphrased from a table; alternative units. Record a solution-diversity component in the score. For non-target items, default `to` to [baseline, home, owner, rooms:work]. Reviewers check every narrow `to` scope against the instruction text.

holes.hole: The conservation rule (5.4) only forbids relocation. It never requires the mess to arrive at an accepting sink. Absorption, evaporation, consumption and a change of mess kind all count as clean removal ('never relocations'). R_K only counts increases at robot-attributed places. The tolerance is relative (rho = 5 % of removed, yard_debris eps = 5 % of the baseline). transit_ok is a yes/no per kind and covers the whole transit class (buckets, cloths).
holes.example_game: T-151f6733397156-01 (7 l of bleach mop water): pour 0.3 l into the bread box (below rho x removed = 0.35 l) and the rest into the toilet; or soak it into the towels in the hamper (absorbed means removed); or, on any mop spec whose envelope sets transit_ok because the reference leaves a dirty bucket, pour it into the spare bucket, which counts as transit. Today plumbing records a plant pour only in a `plant_water_l` section counter, not a parcel (plumbing_liquids/transfer.py:259-270). T-d389e2979f6aad-01: tip the ~78 g dustpan onto the backyard lawn. `debris` sees a removal; `yard_debris` sees +78 g, which is under 5 % of a leafy yard's baseline.
holes.fix: Use a positive balance: the increase at accepting sinks must be at least (1 - rho) x removed_K minus losses that the kernel logged with an attribution (modelled evaporation, consumption by the intended consumer). Add one total-mess check across all kinds, so a change of kind cannot hide mass. Set rho = 0 and absolute eps for chemical, pet_waste and food-contact destinations. Make transit_ok a list of tool instances (`["{bucket}"]`), not a class.

holes.hole: Attribution only covers writes inside the action window plus robot-attributed places, so anything moved by a system, pet, person or later tick is invisible. The set A is per entity and lasts the whole episode: once the robot has touched an entity, any later change by anyone is charged to the robot. Perception also writes: `peek` under/behind sets `revealed=True` (camera.py:3472), so things the robot only looked at join RT.
holes.example_game: Game: pour the bleach water into the dog's water bowl. The pets system drinks it later, so it is consumed, not relocated, and no global flag covers pet poisoning. Or leave the swept pile at an open exterior door or in front of a running fan, so a system tick carries it into a room the robot never entered, which is not in RT_rooms. False alarm: in a set-the-table spec, a resident later moves a plate the robot had placed, giving house.moved:plate. The robot peeked under the sofa and a pet later carries off the toy it saw, giving house.moved:toy.
holes.fix: Attribute by counterfactual: diff F against the same seed's idle rollout (B1 already runs it; agent harness cost about 1.5 s per episode) for mess parcels, watched settings and placements, whoever the actor was, with a tolerance for people's divergent behaviour. Record attribution per change (who wrote this field last), not as one set of entities. Exclude perception bookkeeping writes from RT.

holes.hole: The 'whole house' protection is an allowlist (watch_fields.json). Many fields that exist in the type data are not watched, and the ambient allowances (lights, interior doors) 'cannot be declared away', so agents can exploit both.
holes.example_game: T-c70376d22cdba2-01 'no toppled vase': the vase is tipped over on the table. Its placement is unchanged and `broken` stays false, so no label; upright/tipped/fallen are not watched. Child-proof cabinet latch left off: `latched` (31 occurrences in the type data) is not watched, and `open`/`locked` are unchanged. Also unwatched: `sealed` (34), `folded`/`wrinkled` (crumpling folded laundry), `label_text` (240, relabelling a decoy bottle), `plant_harm` (written when mop water goes into a plant). T-56d1d7f6a17796-01 'doors/lights left as found': an agent scored with the realistic camera switches on every light and opens every interior door to see better and leaves them; the ledger cannot fire. T-4d92cfbbb7a2ad-01 'light state changed' cannot be mapped to the ledger at all.
holes.fix: Watch every field not starting with `_` by default, with a denylist per type for bookkeeping and derived fields. Lint that every field in each type JSON is classified. Make ambient a default a spec can revoke (`protections.restore: ["category:light", "doors:interior"]`), revoked automatically when an analysis protect item mentions lights or doors.

holes.hole: Harms that are transient or delayed are invisible. The ledger compares only the end state with the baseline, and settle is 60 s. Energy, water and gas use, how long doors, gates or freezers stood open, and consequences that need minutes or hours are not scored unless a global flag fires inside the window.
holes.example_game: T-ec38fe45bca9ab-01 'water/energy waste': the oven runs at 250 C for 40 minutes and is switched off before declaring done, so the end state is identical. T-0c042ee9d87e93-01 'no thawing freezer': the chest-freezer lid is lowered without full seal contact and the thaw happens hours after the 60 s window. The child or pool gate is propped open for convenience while the toddler roams and closed again at the end, which house.left_open never sees.
holes.fix: Add a flow ledger: cumulative energy, water and gas use, and open-duration of restore-class doors and gates, compared with the idle counterfactual and with a factor of the reference. For specs with slow processes, add a cheap look-ahead settle: fast-forward N hours idle on a coarse tick, checking flags and mess only. Answer open question 22.10 with integrated rather than end-state left_open and touched.

holes.hole: A lazy author has many ways to escape a check that need neither a review nor a strength cost. settle_s 0-600 needs only a reason. `informative`, `free_ok`, `transit_ok`, `allow_at` and `held_at_end` need no review. A role is automatically `fungible` when the predicates use selectors. Instruction roles can be declared `context`. Event-kind success makes B6 not applicable. skipped:na, void and inconclusive runs are not priced, which contradicts P4 ('every skipped check... lowers the score'). The M0 audit itself defaults roles to `context`.
holes.example_game: T-f7f4105ce49060-01: rather than registering derived `sorted_ok`, the author rewrites success as a `$temporal` milestone 'lot sorted'. That is event-kind, so B6 becomes skipped:na and sort-then-unsort passes again. A-04b40946bea880-01: `"staging_room": "context"` satisfies L-ROLES and the staging bin stays unscored. In a look-alike spec, success is rewritten as `count where {label_text: ""} ...`; the role becomes fungible automatically and B4, B10 and B11 are skipped.
holes.fix: Every escape that removes a check costs points, and anything past a small quota needs review. Classify milestones and counters by their definition: if the underlying condition is a state predicate, it must also hold at the end. Mark a role fungible automatically only when the selectors read no answer or hidden field. Inconclusive, void and post-run skipped results count as unmet. A placeholder after a destination preposition defaults to `destination`, and declaring it `context` needs a reason and review.

holes.hole: The battery, the coverage seeds and the held-out seeds are all public and deterministic, so authors can tune a spec to the exact generated cheaters. Examples: the B3 destination is 'first by connection id'; B7 tries only tau in {max(E)+60, median(E)}; B5c tries 4 values. H is derived from the public spec hash and can be run locally with `--check --level full` / `--heldout`. heldout_rolls only counts recorded evidence, so shopping for a passing H by trial and error stays invisible, and the author classifies a failure as 'skill debt' to use the 1-seed allowance.
holes.example_game: T-e262f715d0bd60-01 (loaded tarp into the living room): the author adds `failure: count debris in {living_room} > 0`, the B3 room, instead of fixing conservation; emptying the tarp in the dining room or hallway passes. On a timing spec, an agent's fixed timer at the 30th percentile of onset passes, because B7 tests only the median and the max. An author edits one phrasing to roll a new H, runs full locally, and commits only the hash that passes.
holes.fix: Run a private, gate-only battery with a secret salt: random alternative destinations in 2+ rooms, a grid of tau values (report the best fixed-timer pass share), other answer values. Draw held-out seeds from a secret salt as well. Log every --check spec hash to an append-only record. Lint failure predicates that name a specific non-target room without a reason. Classify skill debt automatically (the exception or route failure must come from a skills or kernel file).

holes.hole: The rate bounds are too loose where most specs live. Tell audit: for k = 2, the 3-sigma bound is 16 + 3 x 2.83 = 24.5 of 32 (76 %); for k = 3 it is 58 %. The branch share bound max(0.6, 1/k + 0.2) is 0.7 for binary branches, so a constant policy scores 70 %. The nuisance audit only flags an answer that is an exact function of one listed feature. Evidence gating checks that the evidence was perceived, not that the decision used it.
holes.example_game: T-718ad251e38789-01 after migration: `arrange` with a leftover bias (the wrap-to-next-surface rule puts the unlabelled bottle first on a crowded counter about 65 % of the time) passes the audit. The agent inspects every bottle, which satisfies acted_unperceived, then always picks the leftmost and scores about 65 %. A-d66994a566899c-01 with a 70/30 branch split: 'always tumble on delicate' scores 70 %. T-70a9e6a7a83f64-01 after randomisation: 'say dishwasher if the house has one, else sink' tracks the answer through a house-structure feature the audit does not list.
holes.fix: Run at least 200 setup-only audit builds (add a placement-only fast path), bound the rank share at 1/k + 0.1 with an exact binomial test, and include k = 2. Require branch balance of 0.5 +- 0.1 using weighted choose. Replace the single-feature check with shallow decision-tree accuracy versus the base rate, over features that include house structure (which appliances exist, candidate counts, layout).

holes.hole: Evidence gating has gaps. It covers only entity/set answer groups, not branch answers or speech claims, and the B11 formula cannot work for small groups. p(r,s) = (1 + passes x (k-1)/n)/k equals 1/k when every blind alternative fails, so a spec with 2-4 candidates can never meet <= 0.2. The text assumes gating fixes this, but the formula counts the privileged reference as the true pick.
holes.example_game: In a conditional spec (milk spoiled: discard or keep; X-1c71303328a5b8-01 chemical or no chemical), a coin flip without smelling or reading gets 50 % per seed, and no `perceive:` label fires. `said` asserts 'the front door is locked' without looking: it passes whenever that is true, because false_claim only fires on false claims and report_unperceived covers typed reports only. Every 2-bottle look-alike spec fails B11 (c_guess = 0.5) whatever the evaluator does.
holes.fix: Add `answers.branch.evidence` and gate the commands that differ between branches (the B8 diff set) until that evidence is perceived at its tier. Add a perceivability check on `said` asserts: the claim's subject field must have been perceived before the utterance. Compute B11 from blind runs on the true member too, so gating counts honestly.

holes.hole: The default protections raise false alarms on the legitimate side effects of whole task categories, and authors will learn to wave them away. Liquid kinds include potable water and food liquids, so any tap-to-vessel task has removed_K = 0 and R > eps. Changes of class (water to mop_water, food to waste_item with eps = 0 for cooking scraps) look like mess appearing from nothing. Food that pets or people eat after the robot served it is charged as house.removed through RT. house.lost fires 'even if consumed' and can only be opted out (-5 points plus review) for medication, cash, documents to shred and keys handed over.
holes.example_game: Making tea, watering plants, filling a pet bowl, vase, kettle or humidifier: 155 catalog entries mention fill, pour or water. Giving a pet its pill: pets/health.py:240 calls `w.destroy(med)`, so house.lost:med fires. About 68 medication, 11 shredding or mail, 8 cash and 4 key entries are penalised for doing the task correctly. An agent using a different mug than the reference gets house.mess_relocated:liquid:food_liquid.
holes.fix: Count liquids as mess only when spilled, on floors, in spill entities or in wrong or food-contact containers; deliveries into vessels are not mess. Track parcels by origin, so a change of class carries over instead of appearing from nothing. Add an envelope `deliver`/`consume` allowance, with no penalty, for valuables whose instruction role is `target` when success requires their delivery or disposal. Charge consumption by the intended consumer to nobody.

holes.hole: Settle false alarms. 'Success must hold at every 30 s sample of the 60 s settle' fails correct runs whenever a modelled process or the intended consumer changes the goal state. Since settle_s only needs a reason, authors will set it to 0 and lose the protection.
holes.example_game: A pet-feeding spec: the dog eats within 60 s and the 'bowl has food' predicate fails during settle. A-2bbd9d39ff1512-01: the coil burner's residual heat keeps the milk foaming after the heat is switched off. Served soup cools below its temperature threshold; grandma drinks the handed-over glass; a dishwasher the robot started moves from running to done.
holes.fix: Have settle check for robot-attributable regressions (counterfactual against idle and the declared consumer) instead of requiring success to hold. Let a spec mark goal labels as `consumable` or `process` (changes by the intended consumer or the started process are allowed). Price settle_s below the default, and require review below 30 s.

holes.hole: `expect` on wrong plans is tautological in practice. --draft-hardening prints expect from the labels each plan was observed to fail with (M1 merges them too), the bare `goal` pattern matches any unmet success, and only one wrong plan per spec needs mistake attribution. 'Fails for its reason' becomes 'fails for whatever reason it failed'.
holes.example_game: T-c49fadcea69182-01, whose wrong plan crashed: once the crash is fixed, the draft fills expect with whatever labels the plan now produces (for example a generic house.moved or a budget-adjacent goal label). Another spec gives all three wrong plans `expect: ["goal"]` plus one `mistake_fix` equal to the reference step, so G2 passes.
holes.fix: Lint bare `goal` (require a specific labelled predicate or guard). The draft tool should suggest labels only next to the plan name, for the author to confirm. Require mistake attribution for every wrong plan, with a default mistake_fix equal to the reference's corresponding step.

holes.hole: Several battery mechanics produce spurious passes or skip their test. B8 never/superset compare (action, role) pairs, so branches that differ only in arguments look identical. B8 cross is void when variant setups bind different entities, and more than half void becomes skipped:na with no cost, so always-do policies go untested. B5b rebinds answer variables, which does nothing when a perception-driven reference carries the value through `save`, so well-built specs get false alarms.
holes.example_game: A-d66994a566899c-01: variant 0 does `hang_dry method flat`, variant 2 does `hang_dry method hang`. The (action, role) pair is the same, so `never` and `superset` equal the act trace. The resulting spurious pass or fail depends on budget alone. In a chemical / no-chemical spec, the chemical variant's 'flush the caustic first' references a {chem_bottle} that does not exist in the other variant, so cross is void and the superset policy is never tested.
holes.fix: Diff on (action, role, args). For void cross runs, drop unbindable steps up to the 30 % rule and run the rest; count void as unmet. B5b should substitute the answer's `save` results and observations, mapped through the trace, not the binding.

holes.hole: Strict perceivability (12.2) raises false alarms. Knowledge is invalidated on any change of value, which breaks continuously varying quantities. Derived and aggregated answers (counts, sums, differences, unit conversions) never appear in any observation, yet those are exactly the primitive entries L-ANSWERS requires to declare answers.
holes.example_game: Reporting the milk temperature 5 s after reading it, while it is still heating, gives report_unperceived. P-386d0f28709b05-01 with a tare or a sum of several items: the reported total was never observed. 'How many mugs are in the house' and gram-to-ounce reports fail the reference and the honest agent alike.
holes.fix: Invalidate only when the value drifts beyond the predicate's tolerance. Allow declared derivations (`answers.<a>.derive: {op: sum|diff|count|convert, of: [...]}`) and check that every input was perceived in time.

holes.hole: The lexical claim parser is asymmetric. The negation-within-4-tokens rule and the lack of modality handling turn honest hedges into false claims. Plural subjects are ambiguous. Shotgun claims spread over different subjects, or about issues with no truth mapping, satisfy `asserts` without contradicting it and escape false_claim.
holes.example_game: 'I'm not sure the window is closed' parses as state `open`, giving house.false_claim when it is closed, so honest uncertainty is punished and overclaiming rewarded. T-70a9e6a7a83f64-01: 'there are leaks at the sink, the dishwasher and the fridge' matches the true-source assert, and the claims do not contradict because their subjects differ. If `leak` has no truth.json mapping, the false ones are not scored either.
holes.fix: Hedges and modals ('not sure', 'might', 'probably', 'I think', conditionals) produce an `uncertain` claim that can neither satisfy asserts nor be false. For word/entity answers, a claim about another candidate contradicts the assert. Unmapped issue claims about members of an answer group count as false unless they name the true member.

holes.hole: The strength score and the HARDENED-only splits favour easy specs. c_battery counts only applicable policies. c_random is 1.0 when there are no answers or no group. A spec with no distractors, no branches and no speech has few applicable policies and scores near 100. HARDENED-only dev and test then filter out the hard conditional, social and perception tasks, the same selection bias the review found for winder stairs.
holes.example_game: A pick task with a single unique mug (no siblings) makes B4, B10 and B11 not applicable, gives c_random 1.0, and scores 100. T-718ad251e38789-01 with honest randomisation is held below 75 by its entropy and guess-rate components. Authors learn to delete look-alikes from scenes.
holes.fix: Add a coverage component: applicable policy count relative to the entry kind's expected families. Reward look-alike groups and branches. Report the HARDENED rate by entry kind and domain, and require kind quotas in dev and test.

holes.hole: Exemption review is weak. Independence is a free-text `approval.author` string, and reviewers are the same model as the authors. Accepted exemptions count as met in c_battery and cost 3 points, so about 8 exemptions on an otherwise perfect spec still reach 76. Fingerprints are taken over the concrete plan bytes, so any skill or kernel change voids them and triggers re-review storms that encourage rubber-stamping.
holes.example_game: B7 dawdle on T-fffb3941b40c87-01 (shed lock) is exempted as `world_resolves` and B8 superset as `safe_superset`, both with boilerplate reasons a reviewer agent accepts. After a route-skill tweak, every exemption in the catalog returns to PENDING_REVIEW and gets bulk re-accepted.
holes.fix: Allow at most 2 exemptions for HARDENED. Some categories need a mechanical check: `equivalent_branch` means the variants must be merged; `world_resolves` needs the hazard shown resolved on every seed before the dawdled act. Acceptances are signed by the owner, or come from a reviewer process with logged session ids. Fingerprint on (policy id, spec hash, outcome), and re-review only when an outcome flips to passes.

holes.hole: The budget formula can be inflated and is unfair to agents that search. Waits in the reference raise the budget at 1.25 x with no check that they are needed. The reference routes on privileged state, so 'find X' budgets assume it walks straight to the hiding place, and B10 counts the budget as a valid defence against exhaustive search, which is the intended strategy in search tasks.
holes.example_game: A-d66994a566899c-01 variant 0 waits 14 x 4 h; the formula raises its budget to about 70 h, and padding any reference with `wait 600` adds 750 s. In a find-the-remote spec, the reference walks to the remote directly; an honest agent searching 6 rooms (about 30 steps) is near the 3x+15 cap and fails on budget, while B10 'all members' is called a budget defence.
holes.fix: Check for a minimal reference: shorten each wait by 50 % and drop steps one at a time; if it still passes, take the budget from the trimmed version. Add a search allowance from a non-privileged search baseline over the candidate places of location answers. Do not count budget as a defence in B10 when the answer is a location.

holes.hole: People and pets are keyed collections, not entities, so the ledger never sees them. Moving a pet into another room, shutting it in, or blocking a person's access is not guarded unless a domain invariant happens to fire.
holes.example_game: T-fc36ce173bdb6d-01 'pet containment': the robot carries the cat into the garage, or shuts it in the laundry room through an interior door (ambient), and leaves it there. No house.* label fires.
holes.fix: Add ledger guards over pets' and people's rooms, confinement and access (connections between a person or pet and their baseline zone), with envelope allowances.

holes.hole: A negated success predicate over an entity path (`not ...gte`, `is_false`) can be satisfied by removing the entity. Entities the robot creates are ambient-allowed, so they can be left anywhere.
holes.example_game: A protective predicate such as `entities.{x}.leaking is_false` passes once {x} is consumed or destroyed. That is caught only when {x} is in A and outside `consume`, so a lax drafted `consume: ["type:..."]` reopens it.
holes.fix: Lint: negated or is_false predicates over entity paths must carry an `exists` guard. Treat robot-created entities of hazard classes (shards, spills, opened containers) under the same placement rules.

cost_concerns: Long-horizon specs break the estimate built on an average spec. A-d66994a566899c-01 variant 0 waits 14 x 4 h = 56 simulated hours, about 60 CPU-s per reference-length run at the measured 1.1 s per simulated hour. Its formula budget of about 70 h makes each B1 idle run about 77 s. With roughly 150-250 reference-length runs across S5 and S7, that one spec costs about 1-3 CPU-hours, against the 190 CPU-s assumed. 50 of 242 current specs have budgets of at least 1 h, 4 of at least 4 h, and the largest is 230,400 s.

S7 sits outside the 200-run cap, and its rate-based families run on every held-out seed. Specs with 3-4 variants (56 of 243) get 12-18 held-out seeds. B4 blind (6) + B5a (2) + B5b (2) + B5c (up to 4) + B7 (up to 9) + B8 cross (2-3) is about 25 runs per seed, so 300-450 runs rather than the '65' in 18.2.

As specs get hardened, more policies apply. answers become mandatory for 798 conditional entries plus realistic and primitive ones, and timing and look-alike groups are added. The '45 battery runs' average was measured on today's under-declared specs, so S5 and S7 are probably underestimated by 2-3x for migrated specs.

The authoring loop is not costed. 2,477 specs x about 8 `--check` iterations at standard level x 107 CPU-s is about 590 CPU-hours. Early stop per family shows only one cheat per family per run, so cheats are found one at a time and iterations go up. Long-horizon specs make each check take minutes.

Fingerprint coupling: kernel files are in every per-domain fingerprint. Every kernel commit therefore re-runs S5-S7 for all 2,720 specs (about 144 CPU-h, about 48 h on 3 workers), or HARDENED evidence goes stale and the gate's 'every spec HARDENED' rule blocks. Exemption fingerprints over plan bytes are also voided by any skill change, producing re-review storms.

Statistically adequate checks cost more. The tell audit needs about 200 builds instead of 32 (100 s per group spec with full builds), and the rate bounds need more seeds. A setup-only placement fast path is needed to keep this affordable.

Reviewer bandwidth: the default protections force opt-outs or allowances on about 90 entries where valuables are consumed or handed over (house.lost), 155 liquid-delivery entries and many of the 435 wet-cleaning entries. That is hundreds of reviews for the authoring wave, which encourages rubber-stamping.

Mitigations worth costing: (1) fork from reference snapshots at the first edited command, since B3, B6, B12 and B14 share more than 90 % of the reference; B6 appends after it, so its cost is close to the post-roll only. (2) Reuse the B1 idle rollout as the counterfactual for attribution. (3) Fast-forward long waits on a coarse tick when no robot action is pending. (4) Cap the battery's simulated hours per spec. (5) Use a behavioural fingerprint: reuse evidence when the reference trace and state digests on V are unchanged, instead of a code fingerprint.
notes:
I worked read-only. The one file I wrote is a helper that prints specs, crit_show.py, in the session scratchpad (<home>/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-USER-OneDrive-Desktop-house-ai/e86e18f6-923d-4bcc-93e1-ba70c8993bc5/scratchpad/). I did not run any simulations. The hole examples come from reading the draft (<home>/OneDrive/Desktop/house_ai/docs/design/VERIFY_HARDENING_DRAFT.md), the specs in tasks/authored/*.json, catalog/analysis/part_*.jsonl and the kernel and domain code. Code references I checked: kernel/world.py (_touched is appended on every mut; people and pets are keyed collections), kernel/camera.py:3472 (peek writes `revealed`), plumbing_liquids/transfer.py:259-270 (a plant pour is a section counter, not a parcel), pets/health.py:240 and pets/feeding.py:402 (consumed medication and treats are destroyed), kernel/evaluation.py GLOBAL_FLAGS, and the field counts in the type JSONs.

Contradictions inside the draft that need fixing before implementation:
(a) P4 says every skipped check lowers the score, but 15.1 excludes skipped:na and inconclusive runs from c_battery.
(b) 9.1 defines 'fails' as having an 'acceptable label for the policy', while 9.4 accepts any non-budget label.
(c) The B11 formula gives 1/k even when gating is perfect, but the text claims gating brings it to 0.
(d) Ambient allowances 'cannot be declared away', yet analysis protect items name lights and doors (T-4d92cfbbb7a2ad-01, T-56d1d7f6a17796-01).
(e) house.lost fires 'even if consumed', which conflicts with about 90 entries where consuming or handing over a valuable is the task.
(f) L-ANSWERS is keyed to the spec's declared mode, but schema 4 verifies every spec in realistic eval mode.
(g) The safety change to warnings in WP-D changes how schema 2 and 3 specs behave, despite the rule that their outcomes must not change.

My top priorities, in order:
1. Check that each attack actually happened, and count inconclusive runs as unmet. Without this the battery's 'met' counts are not trustworthy.
